'''''Narcissus minor''''', the '''lesser daffodil''' or '''least daffodil''', is a species of ''[[Narcissus (plant)|Narcissus]]'' within the family [[Amaryllidaceae]].<ref name="66111-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:66111-1 |title=''Narcissus minor'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=26 September 2020 }}</ref> The species and its cultivar 'Little Gem' have both gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Narcissus minor'' (13) lesser daffodil |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/11380/Narcissus-minor-(13)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=26 September 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=''Narcissus minor'' 'Little Gem' (1) daffodil 'Little Gem' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/284653/Narcissus-minor-Little-Gem-(1)/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=26 September 2020 }}</ref>

== Description ==
''Narcissus minor'' is a bulb plant which sprouts stems {{convert|8|-|25|cm|in}} tall. Flowers are solitary, yellow in colour and grow between {{convert|25|-|40|mm|in}} long. ''N. minor'' appears very similar to [[Narcissus asturiensis|''N. asturiensis'']]; however, ''N. minor'' possesses larger stems.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Phillips, Rix |first=Roger, Martyn |title=Bulbs Roger Phillips & Martyn Rix |publisher=Pan Books LTD |year=1989 |isbn=0330302531 |pages=122–123}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Narcissus minor'' is [[Native species|native]] to the [[Pyrenees]] mountain range, northern [[Spain]]<ref name=":0" /> and [[France]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2022-05-27 |title=Narcissus minor L. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:66111-1 |access-date=2022-05-27 |website=powo.science.kew.org}}</ref> where it can be found growing in alpine habitat such as mountain meadows and in scrub. This species has also been introduced further into [[Europe]] where it has successfully [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in [[Austria]].<ref name=":1" />
